tables.name: branches
tables.description: Each row is a restaurant outlet or kitchen operated by the chain.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the branch.

columns.name: branch_name
columns.doc: Name of the branch, usually the neighbourhood it serves.

columns.name: format
columns.doc: Outlet format code: 1 = full-service restaurant, 2 = food-court stall, 3 = delivery-only kitchen.

columns.name: seats
columns.doc: Number of customer seats at the branch.

columns.name: opened_on
columns.doc: Date the branch opened, written as YYYY-MM-DD.

tables.name: suppliers
tables.description: Each row is an ingredient supplier used by the chain.

columns.name: supplier_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the supplier.

columns.name: supplier_name
columns.doc: Trading name of the supplier.

columns.name: product_line
columns.doc: Main kind of goods the supplier provides.

columns.name: lead_time
columns.doc: Typical delivery lead time from placing an order to arrival, counted in working days (Monday to Friday).

columns.name: reliability
columns.doc: Percentage of the supplier's deliveries over the past year that arrived on or before the promised date.

tables.name: menu_items
tables.description: Each row is a dish or drink on the menu.

columns.name: item_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the menu item.

columns.name: item_name
columns.doc: Name of the dish or drink as printed on the menu.

columns.name: price
columns.doc: Menu price per serving in Singapore dollars, with 9% GST already included.

columns.name: allergens
columns.doc: Allergen flags added together: 1 = peanuts, 2 = shellfish, 4 = dairy, 8 = gluten, and 0 when none of these apply.

columns.name: supplier_id
columns.doc: Supplier of the dish's main ingredient.

tables.name: orders
tables.description: Each row is a customer order taken at a branch.

columns.name: order_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the order.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Branch that took the order.

columns.name: channel
columns.doc: Order channel code: 1 = dine-in, 2 = takeaway at the counter, 3 = third-party delivery platform, 4 = the chain's own website or app.

columns.name: placed_at
columns.doc: Time the order was placed, in UTC and written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, while the branches keep Singapore time, which is UTC+8.

tables.name: order_lines
tables.description: Each row is a menu item ordered within an order.

columns.name: line_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the order line.

columns.name: order_id
columns.doc: Order the line belongs to.

columns.name: item_id
columns.doc: Menu item that was ordered.

columns.name: qty
columns.doc: Number of servings of the item on the line.

columns.name: discount
columns.doc: Discount given on the line as an amount in Singapore dollars taken off the line total, not a percentage.

tables.name: shifts
tables.description: Each row is a staff shift worked at a branch.

columns.name: shift_id
columns.doc: Numeric ID of the shift.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Branch where the shift was worked.

columns.name: staff_name
columns.doc: Full name of the employee who worked the shift.

columns.name: role
columns.doc: Role code for the shift: 1 = kitchen, 2 = floor service, 3 = bar, 4 = duty manager.

columns.name: shift_date
columns.doc: Calendar date of the shift, written as YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: hours
columns.doc: Hours worked on the shift after deducting the unpaid 30-minute meal break.

columns.name: hourly_rate
columns.doc: Hourly pay rate in Singapore dollars before employer pension contributions.

questions.text: How many orders came in through our own website or app?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE channel = 4

needs_docs.fact: code 4 means the order came through the chain's own website or app

questions.text: Add up the hours worked by our bar staff.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(hours) FROM shifts WHERE role = 3

questions.text: After 10 pm, how many orders did we take?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE CAST(strftime('%H', datetime(placed_at, '+8 hours')) AS INTEGER) >= 22

needs_docs.fact: timestamps are in UTC while the branches keep Singapore time (UTC+8), so 10 pm local is 14:00 in the stored time

questions.text: What is the Chilli Crab's price before tax?
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(price / 1.09, 2) FROM menu_items WHERE item_name = 'Chilli Crab'

needs_docs.fact: the listed price already includes 9% GST, so the pre-tax price is the listed price divided by 1.09

questions.text: In total, how much money did discounts take off our bills?

needs_docs.fact: the discount is an amount in Singapore dollars, not a percentage

questions.text: Which suppliers can deliver within a week?
questions.sql: SELECT supplier_name FROM suppliers WHERE lead_time <= 5 ORDER BY supplier_name

needs_docs.fact: lead time is counted in working days, so one week means at most 5

questions.text: List the suppliers whose deliveries arrive late more than 10% of the time.
questions.sql: SELECT supplier_name FROM suppliers WHERE reliability < 90 ORDER BY supplier_name

needs_docs.fact: reliability is the percentage of deliveries that arrived on time, so late more than 10% of the time means below 90

questions.text: Tell me which dishes have shellfish in them.
questions.sql: SELECT item_name FROM menu_items WHERE (allergens & 2) > 0 ORDER BY item_name

needs_docs.fact: allergen flags are added together and the value 2 stands for shellfish

questions.text: Which branch has the most seats?
questions.sql: SELECT branch_name FROM branches ORDER BY seats DESC LIMIT 1

questions.text: Show me everything on the menu that comes from Golden Wok Noodles.
questions.sql: SELECT m.item_name FROM menu_items m JOIN suppliers s ON s.supplier_id = m.supplier_id WHERE s.supplier_name = 'Golden Wok Noodles' ORDER BY m.item_name

readings.sql: SELECT b.branch_name FROM branches b JOIN orders o ON o.branch_id = b.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, b.branch_name LIMIT 1
SELECT b.branch_name FROM branches b JOIN orders o ON o.branch_id = b.branch_id JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY b.branch_id ORDER BY SUM(l.qty) DESC, b.branch_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Branch busyness is measured by how many orders the branch has taken.

readings.sql: SELECT m.item_name FROM menu_items m JOIN order_lines l ON l.item_id = m.item_id GROUP BY m.item_id ORDER BY SUM(l.qty) DESC, m.item_name LIMIT 1

readings.gloss: highest sales value at menu price
readings.sql: SELECT m.item_name FROM menu_items m JOIN order_lines l ON l.item_id = m.item_id GROUP BY m.item_id ORDER BY SUM(l.qty * m.price) DESC, m.item_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Dishes are ranked by servings sold, not by sales value.

readings.sql: SELECT supplier_name FROM suppliers ORDER BY reliability DESC, supplier_name LIMIT 1
SELECT supplier_name FROM suppliers ORDER BY lead_time ASC, supplier_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Supplier quality is judged by on-time delivery percentage, the higher the better.

readings.gloss: what the guest pays, after line discounts
readings.sql: SELECT SUM(m.price * l.qty - l.discount) FROM order_lines l JOIN menu_items m ON m.item_id = l.item_id WHERE l.order_id = 1004
SELECT SUM(m.price * l.qty) FROM order_lines l JOIN menu_items m ON m.item_id = l.item_id WHERE l.order_id = 1004

resolving_note.text: The cost of an order means what the guest actually pays, so line discounts are subtracted from menu price times quantity.

ambiguous.text: Who is our hardest-working team member?

readings.sql: SELECT staff_name FROM shifts GROUP BY staff_name ORDER BY SUM(hours) DESC, staff_name LIMIT 1
SELECT staff_name FROM shifts GROUP BY staff_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, staff_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Work effort is compared by total hours worked, not by the number of shifts.
